editorial:
Forget everything you know about the jolly old man in the red suit. You are diving into a twisted version of Christmas that feels more like a nightmare than a fairy tale. Based on a poem by Neil Gaiman, this short film shows you a Santa who is not interested in giving toys to good kids. Instead, he is a scary figure who hunts down those who have been naughty. The vibe is dark, creepy, and a bit weird, making it feel like a forbidden bedtime story that you cannot stop watching once it starts.

The animation style is unique and adds to the spooky mood, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you want a big action movie. The best part is how it flips the script on a holiday tradition, giving you a real chill down your spine. If you love dark fantasy, you should definitely track this down. You can find it for rent on Apple TV or check if it is available for streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture quality. It is a quick watch that will leave you thinking twice about leaving your door unlocked on Christmas Eve.
endingExplained: The movie ends by showing that Santa is actually a terrifying monster who collects the naughty children. Instead of a magical sleigh ride, the final scenes reveal his true, scary form. He doesn't bring gifts; he brings punishment. The twist is that the joy of the holiday is just a cover for his dark work. Everything wraps up with the realization that no one is safe if they have been bad.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark twists on classic holiday stories.
